Thank you, that is a very good question, and I want to be careful with my answer. Our results suggest that the drug may reduce nerve pain, but this is a preliminary finding. We had only forty patients, so it is possible that the effect is smaller in a bigger group. It seems that the patients with recent symptoms responded better, but I am not one hundred percent sure yet, because the two groups were not the same size. So my honest answer is this: it probably works for some patients, and it is unlikely to work for everybody. We need a second study before we can make a strong claim. If you are interested, I can share the data with you after the session.

I see your point, and I think your data is really interesting. But I am not sure we can say that the treatment works. In my opinion, the improvement might be related to the placebo effect, because the patients knew they were getting a new drug. It could also be a question of dosage. You used a high dose, and in our clinic, patients generally cannot take that dose for a long time. So I would say the results are promising, but probably not conclusive for now. Maybe the next step is a trial where the patients and the doctors do not know who gets the real drug.
